title: arXiv Mathematics — daily batch, 2026-11-02
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This is an inferred ordering of notable recent papers, not a readership or download ranking; the papers are very recent and citation/attention evidence is limited.

sections.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
sections.abstract: The authors prove fast Potts Glauber mixing for every number of states throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regimes on random regular graphs and lattice cubes or tori, and also obtain logarithmic-time Swendsen–Wang mixing on random regular graphs.
sections.claimed_result: In Theorems 1.1–1.2, for fixed q≥2, the authors prove O(n(log n)^κ) mixing with high probability on uniformly random Δ-regular graphs below β_u(q,T_Δ), inverse spectral gap n^(1+o(1)) on d-dimensional cubes or tori below β_c(q,Z^d), and O(log n) Swendsen–Wang mixing on random regular graphs throughout uniqueness.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Ferromagnetic q-state Potts model; uniformly sampled simple Δ-regular graphs in the first result, cubes or tori in Z^d in the second, and temperature strictly below the stated uniqueness/critical threshold.
sections.unique_caveat: The random-regular-graph result is high-probability for that graph ensemble, not every bounded-degree graph. On lattices, the inverse-gap estimate gives n^(2+o(1)) mixing, while the authors expect O(n log n) and do not prove it.

sections.title: A Counterexample to the Alon-Krivelevich Conjecture and a New Lower Bound for Choosability of Bipartite Graphs
sections.abstract: The authors construct bipartite graphs whose list-chromatic number grows asymptotically faster than the logarithm of maximum degree, disproving the Alon–Krivelevich conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: For integers k≥2 and r²>2(2k−1)ln(2k−1), the constructed bipartite graph is not colorable from its standard lists, yielding ch(G)≥(1/32−o(1))(ln Δ)²/(ln ln Δ)³ and hence ch(G)/ln Δ→∞ along the family.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple bipartite graphs with vertex classes copies of the k-subsets of a (2k−1)-element set; adjacency is defined by intersection size at most r, and each vertex list is its corresponding subset.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a lower bound for the constructed family, not an asymptotic characterization of its true choosability; the authors note that the actual value may be larger.

sections.title: Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation
sections.abstract: For rotationally invariant continuum first-passage percolation in dimension at least two, the authors establish exponential concentration on a sub-square-root scale and infer a variance bound of order at most n^(1−ε).
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives exponential concentration for the smoothed-Gaussian density at scale |x|^(1/2(1−ε)); Theorem 1.2 extends it to the stated general-density assumptions and implies Var[T(0,x)]≤C'|x|^(1−ε).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Continuum first-passage percolation in R^d, d≥2; the general theorem assumes a measurable, uniformly positive and bounded, locally determined density equivariant under rigid motions, driven by Gaussian white noise or a homogeneous Poisson process.
sections.unique_caveat: This does not solve the lattice version of Kesten's question; the introduction says that question remains open, and a related companion-paper observation requires a nondegenerate C²,α time-constant condition not known for any weight distribution.

sections.title: Tiling without a subspace complement: a sharp counterexample in dimension nine over the field with two elements
sections.abstract: The authors exhibit a 64-point subset of F₂⁹ that tiles by translation but has no linear-subspace tiling complement, establishing a sharp dimension threshold for the existence of such complements.
sections.claimed_result: Every nonempty translational tile in F₂^d has a linear-subspace complement exactly when d≤8; the dimension-nine example has 512 tiling complements and 64 spectra, each classification forming one translation class.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite vector spaces over F₂; tiling means unique translational factorization of the whole group. The example is spectral and is not a counterexample to Fuglede's conjecture.
sections.unique_caveat: The positive assertion in dimension eight for the remaining 16-point case relies on the authors' earlier theorem based on classifying perfect binary codes of length fifteen.

sections.title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations
sections.abstract: The authors use Dirichlet-form methods to construct stochastic thin-film dynamics, prove existence and uniqueness of the evolution of laws, and establish tightness and convergence results for spatial discretizations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish existence and uniqueness for the law-valued evolution and regularity of process realizations; in a Gaussian-reference, non-degenerate-mobility case they identify an energy solution, prove uniform tightness of Galerkin and spectral approximations, and establish Mosco convergence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Overdamped gradient-flow model of a thin liquid film with thermal noise. The Dirichlet-form construction uses a Gibbsian equilibrium measure, giving a (1+1)-dimensional setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The need for an available Gibbsian equilibrium measure limits the treatment to one spatial dimension; the energy-solution characterization and Mosco convergence are stated for a simplified Gaussian-reference, non-degenerate-mobility case.

sections.title: Landscape Intervals: A Geometric Framework for Multiparameter Persistence Landscapes
sections.abstract: The authors define landscape intervals and derive stable multiparameter persistence-landscape invariants that generalize existing one- and multiparameter constructions, with a numerical framework illustrated on mesh and medical-image data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove recovery of Bubenik's landscapes in the one-parameter case and encompass Vipond's multiparameter landscapes; they establish two exact erosion-distance identities and perturbation stability, refine interleaving-stability bounds, and show finite-information recovery for a specified class of modules.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Persistence modules indexed by a multiparameter space; finite-information recovery applies only to a certain class of modules, and the numerical workflow is illustrated on surface meshes and medical images.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not claim finite-information recovery for arbitrary multiparameter modules, and the data examples are illustrations rather than broad empirical validation.

sections.title: Maximum of the Two-Dimensional Directed Polymer in the Critical Window
sections.abstract: For a two-dimensional directed polymer in a Gaussian environment at critical-window inverse temperature, the authors prove that the maximum log partition function over a square of side order √N, divided by √log N, converges in probability to 2√2.
sections.claimed_result: For every fixed real ϑ, with β_N=√((1−ϑ/log N)/R_N) and R_N∼(log N)/π, the maximum 𝔐_N of log Z_N(x) over |x|∞≤√N satisfies 𝔐_N/√(log N)→2√2 in probability.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional lattice directed polymer, Gaussian environment, critical-window scaling as above, and maximum over starting points in the specified box.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a first-order in-probability asymptotic in this Gaussian two-dimensional scaling; it does not state a fluctuation law for the centered maximum or cover other environments and dimensions.
